workflow: Locate the target, configuration and earliest failing action. Separate compiler, linker and UBT failures and choose the narrowest authorized check.
Determine whether the task needs a commandlet, editor, game or packaged executable. Define the observable output and capture process status and the relevant log.
Start at a failure signature, then trace backward to its first meaningful cause. Keep the surrounding context and separate shutdown fallout.
Define the size metric, platform and representative build. Attribute the largest contributors before choosing a code, content, shader or delivery change.
Identify costly binaries and their module or plugin dependencies. Change one dependency at a time and compare retained features and size.
Compare cooked assets with the exercised use set. Trace references and explicit keep rules before narrowing cook scope.
Measure container size separately from download size. Compare chunk boundaries, compression and the bytes sent by the distribution host.
Use the same build configuration and delivery unit for both measurements. Attribute bytes to containers, packages or binaries before interpreting the difference.
Inventory target formats, material quality levels and permutations. Check affected materials on the target hardware after narrowing a permutation set.
Match the validation to the cut. Include representative startup, loading and gameplay coverage as well as byte counts.
Identify the actor, control or socket and the relevant frame range. Choose the motion trail, time posing or pivot operation and inspect the resulting trajectory.
Determine if the sequence owns the object or refers to an existing one. Inspect binding IDs, tags and overrides before changing a binding.
Resolve the camera binding and camera-cut section separately. Check the active cut and focal settings on the requested frames.
Find the rig track, section and named control. Confirm the coordinate space and frame before keying and sample the resulting pose.
Identify the sequence, binding, track and section from the outermost object inward. Check the sequence time base before interpreting frame ranges.
Resolve the sequence's Director Blueprint and the event endpoint. Check the bound object, parameter signature and track trigger together.
Trace how gameplay starts the sequence and which runtime object receives its events. Verify the event track and Director endpoint agree.
Choose the interchange format and target binding. Match frame range and transform conventions and compare the result with the source take.
Find the intended section and typed channel. Convert display frames to its time base and read back the keys and interpolation around the edit.
Trace explicit navigation rules, focus handlers and widget hierarchy. Diagram reachable focus destinations and mark paths that need runtime observation.
Choose an Editor Utility Widget parent, build its widget tree and bind editor actions. Verify how it opens as an editor tab.
Record repro input and the expected widget state. Distinguish layout, visibility and input routing using the live widget hierarchy in the authorized session.
Identify both asset revisions or actor instances. Use the diff operation advertised for that asset type and report the property or graph changes.
Determine the target level and intended placement surface. Account for the actor pivot and bounds before deciding whether to ground it.
Resolve the asset's content path and query its provider state and revision history. Compare the requested revisions before considering any checkout or submit.
Inspect the widget class and parent slot separately. Read their exposed properties before setting layout values and check the resulting hierarchy.
Resolve the asset kind and active builder. Inspect the node interfaces and pin types, then verify the resulting connections and output.
Identify the target page and platform assignment before editing. Compare the page with its default and check which page the target will use.
Inventory simultaneous wave players, nested graphs and platform pages. Profile the costly branch before changing playback or graph complexity.
Select the parent graph and inspect the inputs supported by its preset. Apply the requested defaults and check which settings still inherit.
Choose a pattern that matches the intended sound. Resolve node and pin interfaces from the installed build before wiring the pattern.
Trace each trigger from start to finish, including fan-in and feedback. Check the finished signal and graph validity after rewiring.
Decide whether the task needs a new graph, a preset, inspection or an edit. Open the corresponding asset and verify its interface before applying that workflow.
Check which deformer model and training resources the build provides. Match the skeletal mesh, training inputs and evaluation asset before comparing deformation.
Inspect graph branches, collections, modifiers and variables. Trace each requested render layer to its output before changing a graph.
Inspect the queue's jobs, shots, configuration and output locations. Verify resolved per-shot settings before starting any requested render.
Resolve the ViewModel instance, field paths and binding direction. Check data types and change notification on the source field.
Determine whether the task concerns runtime setup, output validation, profiling or manual edits. Inspect the owning component before choosing a specialist workflow.
Trace the execution source, grid and node data for one failing location. Check which part ran on the CPU or GPU before interpreting the output.
Trace a generated instance to its owning component. Apply persistent edits at the supported edit layer or generating graph and check behavior across regeneration.
Profile a representative generation source and grid. Locate repeated work and CPU/GPU transfers before comparing a targeted graph change.
Identify the surface, generation source, grid and output footprint. Select a setup that matches the terrain representation.
Trace landscape height and grass inputs to point generation and mesh spawning. Check coverage against one landscape component first.
Identify MeshTerrain tiles and the surface data the runtime graph can consume. The inspected Epic entry is a placeholder, so verify any proposed setup in the project.
Check source activation, grid alignment and coverage in a representative area. Trace missing output back to the first empty stage.
Compare grass coverage with grid placement, landscape textures and density. Confirm the graph resolves the intended mesh set.
Compare the PCG grid with tile boundaries and component coverage. The inspected entry leaves further MeshTerrain-specific checks open.
Inspect the target device's memory, sampler and shader limits. Scale runtime generation and compare coverage and frame cost on that device.
Fix the viewpoint and capture settings for comparison. Choose the diagnostic pass that separates lighting, geometry or material causes and compare the same region.
Inspect the skeletal binding and overlapping animation layers. Check priorities, blend weights and the pose at the overlap.
Identify the intended focused widget. Prefer a complete press/release gesture for a click or key and verify which widget received it.
Inspect the available node interfaces and actual pin types. Trace the requested output's dependencies and verify its resolution and format before baking.
Resolve the Wasm and WebGPU target, browser requirements and hosting headers. Check packaged resources, loading and the first rendered frame.
Choose a device tier, renderer preset and repeatable scene. Measure one performance change at a time under the same browser conditions.
Inventory the intended BC and ASTC payloads. Check that browser capability selection requests the matching texture set and that both variants are served.
Find the animation on the Widget Blueprint and the widget it binds. Check the section, channel and playback timing against the intended property.
Gather the widget tree, slots, bindings and animations. Record each finding against its widget path and identify runtime-only behavior.
